stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: The textbook model predicts that raising a minimum wage will reduce employment. That prediction assumes, however, that workers can easily move to rival employers. Where a single firm does most of the local hiring, it can hold wages down by hiring fewer people than it needs, and a wage floor removes the payoff from that restraint, so employment can rise rather than fall. ______ a state labor commission recommended raising the minimum wage only in counties where one employer accounted for more than half of local jobs, leaving the rate unchanged in counties with many competing firms.
explanation: The sentence before the blank explains a mechanism: where one employer dominates hiring, a wage floor can raise employment instead of lowering it. The sentence after the blank describes a decision that depends on that mechanism. The commission raised the wage only where one employer dominates and left it unchanged everywhere else. If you put 'so' in the blank, it reads naturally: the mechanism works only in single-employer markets, so the commission targeted only those markets. 'For this reason' expresses that cause-and-effect relationship.

A.why: You noticed that the recommendation goes against the textbook prediction in the first sentence, and that is true. But the blank links the recommendation to the sentence right before it, which describes the single-employer mechanism, and the recommendation does not contradict that sentence. It acts on it. You matched the new sentence to the wrong sentence and read a surprising result as a disagreement.

B.why: The commission's recommendation is not an instance of employment rising after a wage increase. It is a policy that someone chose because of the principle. You confused an example of the rule with the result of applying the rule. The commission used the reasoning to decide what to do, so the sentence is a consequence, not an illustration.

D.why: 'Similarly' says the next sentence describes a parallel case. The recommendation is not a second case like the first one. It is an action that follows from the mechanism just described, so it needs a cause-and-effect word, not an addition word.

subtype_name: Result of what came before (Thus / Hence / For this reason / As such)

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Longleaf pine seedlings spend years as low tufts of needles, and during that stage they face two kinds of competitors: hardwood shrubs, which shade them from above, and dense grasses, which crowd their roots. Fire checks both, since thick sheaths of needles shield the seedlings' growing tips while the competitors burn back. ______ managers of the Corley Flats preserve set low-intensity fires every two to three years, timing most burns for early summer, when the hardwood shrubs are actively growing and least able to recover.
explanation: The sentences before the blank set out a need and a mechanism. The seedlings face competitors, and fire suppresses those competitors while sparing the seedlings. The sentence after the blank describes what managers do because of that: they burn on a regular schedule and time the fires to hit the shrubs hardest. If you put 'so' in the blank, the passage holds together. 'Hence' signals that the managers' practice is a result of the mechanism described.

A.why: The passage names two competitors, and the sentence after the blank mentions only one of them, the hardwood shrubs. That made it look as though the sentence zooms in on one member of the group. But 'Specifically' needs the next sentence to restate the previous one more precisely, and a burn schedule is not a sharper version of 'fire checks both competitors.' It is an action taken because of that fact.

B.why: 'Afterward' sets up a sequence in time, as if the managers' burns came after the fire described in the previous sentence. That sentence is not an event, though. It is a general explanation of how fire affects the plants. The burns follow from that explanation logically, not chronologically.

D.why: 'Even so' means the next sentence goes ahead despite what came before. Nothing in the passage argues against burning. The passage explains why fire helps the seedlings, so the managers' burns agree with it. You read the deliberate setting of fires as surprising, but the passage has already explained why it makes sense.
